sections.content: How many people are "beauticians and related occupations"?

93,010 people

were counted on the census as "beauticians and related occupations" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Beauticians and related workers give facial and body beauty treatments, apply cosmetics and dress wigs.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "beauticians and related occupations" there were more women than men (90.3% compared with 9.7%).

This means "beauticians and related occupations" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "leisure, travel and related personal service occupations".

Men made up 9.7% and women made up 90.3% of "beauticians and related occupations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "beauticians and related occupations" included:

  • receptionists
  • higher level teaching assistants
  • occupational therapists

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "beauticians and related occupations", 19.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "beauticians and related occupations" was 65 years or older.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "beauticians and related occupations" included:

  • data analysts
  • actuaries, economists and statisticians
  • web design professionals

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "beauticians and related occupations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "beauticians and related occupations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "beauticians and related occupations", 9.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (66.7% compared with 33.3%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (64.1%) than an employee (35.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
